subject.title: Cron consecutiveErrors increments on gateway-restart interruptions, masking real agent-failure rate (post-#50414)

question: Should gateway-restart recovery reuse the existing `skipped` cron status with neutral counters and delivery, or should OpenClaw add a distinct public `interrupted` terminal status and associated counter semantics?
rationale: Both options alter persisted status vocabulary and the operator-facing meaning of cron health, retries, notifications, and integrations; code review alone cannot choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Reuse `skipped` for restart interruption
options.body: Persist the restart diagnostic as a skipped run, leave failure counters unchanged, and avoid a failure-delivery attempt; this is the smaller API surface.

options.title: Add `interrupted` as a terminal status
options.body: Expose a separate public status and interruption counter so operators can distinguish planned gateway interruption from both skipped work and agent failure.

recommendation.title: Reuse `skipped` for restart interruption
recommendation.body: Persist the restart diagnostic as a skipped run, leave failure counters unchanged, and avoid a failure-delivery attempt; this is the smaller API surface.

likelyOwner.reason: Their current related recovery work is closest to the durable cron restart boundary, though final status semantics need broader maintainer sponsorship.
